name: GET /api/leadflow/consent/overview - receipts, suppressions and the purpose taxonomy for #view-consent
description:
The one call behind the Consent & Preferences screen: the receipt register, the six KPI tiles, the suppression controls and the purpose taxonomy.

THE TASK NAMED THREE ENDPOINTS THAT DO NOT EXIST, and this composes the ones that do. sdk-consent serves /api/consents/* (PLURAL) and has never served /api/consent/*: there is no GET /api/consent/receipts and no GET /api/consent/purposes. The same singular/plural slip is what made the AI coach's recording gate deny every call for weeks, so every path here was taken from packages/sdk-consent/src/server/routes.ts rather than from a description.

RECEIPTS COME FROM /api/consents/export, which is a DSAR export rather than a register, and that difference is stated instead of hidden. It answers per person_id, so a tenant-wide register is assembled rather than read - which is why the register is capped and reports `truncated` when it hits the cap. A screen that silently shows the first N receipts of an unknown total invites somebody to conclude that is all of them.

THE EXPIRING WINDOW IS A PARAMETER, defaulting to 30 days (AC1). Out-of-range or unparseable values are REJECTED rather than defaulted, because quietly substituting 30 would let a reader compare a figure they believe covers a quarter against one that covers a month.

SUPPRESSION COUNTS ARE RECONCILED, NOT ASSUMED (AC2). The response reports the provider's own count beside ours and a `reconciled` flag per channel. Where they disagree the screen must say so: a suppression list that has drifted from the provider is the exact condition under which somebody gets messaged after opting out, and a single merged number would conceal it.

THE PURPOSE TAXONOMY CANNOT BE READ, AND THE SCREEN SAYS SO. AC4 asks for the taxonomy to render from the REGISTERED purposes rather than a hard-coded list. sdk-consent exposes only POST /api/consents/purposes, which registers one - there is no GET, so the registry cannot be listed. The response therefore returns purposes:[] with a purpose_taxonomy_gap naming the missing endpoint, and the screen renders that state rather than a constant. Deriving the list from purposes seen on existing receipts was considered and rejected: it would omit any registered purpose nobody has consented to yet, which is precisely when a taxonomy panel earns its place. Raised in ProjexCloud docs/handoff.

DEGRADES PER PANEL. Each upstream read answers independently, so deliverability being down empties the suppression controls and leaves the register readable. upstream_available reports each separately and an empty result is never conflated with an unreachable one.

requiresRole:["privacy_officer"] and NO testCase pins an Authorization header (MUST-71). Consent receipts name a person, a purpose and what they were told; the Privacy Officer owns the lawful-basis question. QA: depends on register and login.

testCases.name: The overview composes every panel and reports availability per source
The expiring window is honoured when given explicitly
NEGATIVE: an unparseable window is rejected rather than silently defaulted to 30
NEGATIVE: a window outside the supported range is rejected

errorCases.message: expiring_within_days must be an integer between 1 and 365
errorCases.when: the window is non-numeric or out of range. Rejected rather than defaulted so two readings are never silently measured over different periods.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the header is absent or not Bearer. Not authored as a testCase: pinning it would defeat the role swap (MUST-71).

errorCases.message: No policy grants this action to the caller's roles.
errorCases.when: the caller does not hold consent.purpose_manage. Not reachable while this definition runs under requiresRole.
